newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount denies wanting to delay offer.
newsitem.headline: Discount denies wanting to delay offer.

text.p: A spokeswoman for Israel Discount Bank on Tuesday denied newspaper reports that the bank preferred to delay an offering of shares and warrants until April.
"Nobody spoke to us," the spokeswoman said about the newspaper reports, adding, "We are working hard to complete it on time."
The Israeli financial daily Globes reported that Discount's management preferred to delay the offering until April rather than base it on estimates for its fourth-quarter debt provision and earnings.

Globes said the bank did not want to take responsibility for estimating the fourth-quarter provision and profits in order to publish the prospectus before the end of February. Discount told the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange last week the provision would be considerably bigger than previous quarters.

The offering of shares and warrants in the bank held by the government was due to be made this week, but last Thursday Discount reported the Securities Authority said it would not approve the prospectus without fourth-quarter figures.

Discount has until the end of February to publish a prospectus based on its third-quarter results. After that, it will have to wait until it can include its fourth-quarter earnings, which are not expected to come out until March.
The Discount spokeswoman said the bank "continued to work" on the prospectus but would provide no further details.

A spokesman for the Securities Authority would not comment on the matter, and the managing director of MI Holdings, the government company charged with selling the state's bank shares, was unavailable for comment.
The offering is for 17 percent of Discount, Israel's third-largest bank, with a market value of about 600 million shekels.
